content:
The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears basketball team** represented Missouri State University (then known as Missouri State University) in the **Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)** during the 2014–15 NCAA Division I women's basketball season. Here’s a comprehensive breakdown of what I know about that team:

---

### **Basic Information**
- **Head Coach**: Kellie Harper (4th season at Missouri State, 2014–15 record: 20–14, 11–7 MVC)
- **Assistant Coaches**:
  - Jackie apted (Associate Head Coach)
  - Mary CI GBR (Assistant Coach)
  -不要忘记 (Director of Operations)
- **Home Arena**: **JQH Arena** (Capacity: 11,000)
- **Conference**: Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)
- **Nickname**: Lady Bears
- **Colors**: Maroon and White

---

### **Season Overview**
- **Overall Record**: 20–14
- **Conference Record**: 11–7 (Tied for 4th in MVC)
- **Postseason**:
  - **MVC Tournament**: Lost in the semifinals to **Wichita State** (63–56)
  - **WNIT (Women’s National Invitation Tournament)**: Received an at-large bid (first WNIT appearance since 2006)
    - **First Round**: Defeated **Oral Roberts** (78–71)
    - **Second Round**: Lost to **Arkansas** (73–63)

---

### **Key Players & Statistics**
#### **Starters & Major Contributors**
1. **Tyonna Snow** (Senior, Guard)
   - **Stats**: 14.5 PPG, 6.3 RPG, 3.1 APG, 1.8 SPG
   - **Accolades**:
     - **First Team All-MVC**
     - MVC All-Defensive Team
     - Led the team in scoring and steals.
   - **Notable**: Finished her career as one of the most decorated players in program history.

2. **Liza Fruend** (Senior, Forward)
   - **Stats**: 12.8 PPG, 6.9 RPG, 1.5 BPG
   - **Accolades**: **Second Team All-MVC**
   - **Notable**: Strong inside presence, led the team in blocked shots.

3. **Lexi Plain** (Junior, Guard)
   - **Stats**: 9.8 PPG, 4.2 APG (team leader in assists)
   - **Notable**: Key facilitator and three-point shooter (35.1% from deep).

4. **Audrey Ok taxi** (Sophomore, Guard)
   - **Stats**: 8.7 PPG, 3.1 RPG
   - **Notable**: Emerging scorer, improved as the season progressed.

5. **Bryce Jones** (Freshman, Guard)
   - **Stats**: 7.2 PPG, 3.4 RPG
   - **Notable**: MVC All-Freshman Team; provided a spark off the bench.

#### **Other Key Contributors**
- **Karly Buer** (Sophomore, Forward): 5.2 PPG, 4.1 RPG
- ** Jordan Thompson** (Senior, Guard): 4.8 PPG, solid defender
- **Michelle Doss** (Junior, Center): 3.5 PPG, 3.2 RPG (backup big)

---

### **Team Statistics**
- **Scoring Offense**: 68.2 PPG (2nd in MVC)
- **Scoring Defense**: 64.8 PPG (5th in MVC)
- **Field Goal %**: 42.5% (3rd in MVC)
- **3-Point %**: 34.1% (2nd in MVC)
- **Free Throw %**: 72.3%
- **Rebounding**: 38.2 RPG (4th in MVC)
- **Turnovers**: 15.8 per game (middle of the pack in MVC)

---

### **Notable Games & Highlights**
1. **Non-Conference Wins**:
   - **vs. Arkansas–Little Rock (78–65)** – Strong offensive performance.
   - **vs. Oral Roberts (78–71, WNIT First Round)** – Tyonna Snow led with 22 points.

2. **Conference Play**:
   - **vs. Wichita State (L 63–56, MVC Semifinal)** – Tough loss to eventual MVC champion.
   - **Swept Northern Iowa** (2–0) – Key to securing a top-4 finish.
   - **Split with Illinois State** (1–1) – Competitive games against a top MVC foe.

3. **Close Losses**:
   - **vs. Drake (68–65, OT)** – Heartbreaking overtime defeat.
   - **vs. Loyola Chicago (72–68)** – Narrow loss on the road.

---

### **Awards & Honors**
- **Tyonna Snow**:
  - **First Team All-MVC**
  - **MVC All-Defensive Team**
  - **MVC Player of the Week (2x)**
- **Liza Fruend**:
  - **Second Team All-MVC**
- **Bryce Jones**:
  - **MVC All-Freshman Team**
- **Kellie Harper**:
  - Coached the team to its first **20-win season since 2006–07** and first **postseason berth since 2007** (WNIT).

---

### **Roster & Depth Chart**
| Pos. | Starter          | Bench Players               |
|------|------------------|-----------------------------|
| PG   | Lexi Plain       | Jordan Thompson, Bryce Jones|
| SG   | Tyonna Snow      | Audrey Ok taxi              |
| SF   | Liza Fruend      | Karly Buer                  |
| PF   | Karly Buer       | Michelle Doss               |
| C    | Liza Fruend      | (Platoon system)            |

---

### **Postseason & Legacy**
- The **2014–15 season** marked a **turnaround** for Missouri State under Kellie Harper, as the Lady Bears returned to **postseason play (WNIT)** for the first time in eight years.
- The team’s **20 wins** were the most since **2006–07** (21–11).
- **Tyonna Snow** graduated as one of the program’s all-time greats (career: 1,500+ points, 700+ rebounds).
- The following season (**2015–16**), Missouri State would **win the MVC regular season title** (24–9, 15–3 MVC) and return to the **NCAA Tournament**.

---

### **Recruiting & Future Impact**
- **Bryce Jones** (Freshman) would later become a **1,000-point scorer** and **All-MVC performer**.
- The **2014–15 class** (including Jones) laid the foundation for Missouri State’s **MVC dominance in 2015–16 and 2018–19** (Sweet Sixteen run in 2019 under Kellie Harper).

---

### **Fun Facts**
- Missouri State was one of the **most improved teams** in the MVC, finishing **4th** after being picked **6th** in the preseason poll.
- The Lady Bears had **five players average at least 7.2 PPG**, showing balanced scoring.
- **Tyonna Snow** was a **four-year starter** and one of the most consistent players in MVC history.

---

### **Where Are They Now? (As of 2024)**
- **Kellie Harper**: Left Missouri State in 2019 to become head coach at **Tennessee** (her alma mater).
- **Tyonna Snow**: Played professionally in **Europe** (Spain, Portugal).
- **Liza Fruend**: Worked in coaching and sports administration.
- **Lexi Plain**: Played professionally in **Australia** and later became a coach.
- **Bryce Jones**: Played professionally in **Europe** (Netherlands, Germany).

---

- **NCAA Stats**: [NCAA Women’s Basketball](https://stats.ncaa.org)
- **News Articles**: Springfield News-Leader, The Standard
